rows.what the ink shows: The deleted symbol has a small two-lobed bowl above the horizontal cancellation and a distinct stem descending well below it. The bowl survives on both sides of the stem; a T would not supply those curved upper lobes.

After the compressed low initial run, the f rises to a sharp upper turn and drops deeply below the marginal baseline. A small raised angular t follows immediately. There is no intervening low o loop or r/m group between f and the raised terminal. The larger loop farther right belongs to the original horizontal text crossing the margin line.

The cancellation leaves an initial i-dot and a small following loop, low middle returns, a tall narrow descending f-like stroke near the right, and a short accent above the ending. The heavy horizontal stroke merges the intervening bodies, so the entire sequence identifiée is not securely recoverable from the remaining strokes.

Immediately before the surviving (A), a small upper peak and a short lower return protrude from the cancellation. The central connected bodies are merged into the strikeout; neither a complete initial d loop/ascender nor the final letter sequence can be distinguished.

The measure glyph has a long left leg descending below the upper writing level, then retraces upward to a short right shoulder/return. It is not a simple open v-shaped pair of arms. A separate lower-right A has two upright sides and a short crossbar.

The sigma has a clear small oval left body and a horizontal upper-right stroke, followed by (A). A dense vertical smear occupies the superscript position and touches the sigma ending. Enlargement and contrast show no separable crossed star arms; the smear also prevents establishing that the position was blank.

The unstruck symbol has a broad curved bowl, open at the upper left and closing into a small right loop, with a long stem descending from the bowl junction. These curved bowl strokes distinguish it from the straight cap and stem of T.
